At a glance

A modern loft, priced below its reference values

The loft costs 4% less per m² than Berlin's city-centre average and 11% less than Berlin new-build. It sits on the fifth floor with access to a roof terrace, in a city where only 0.3% of multi-family housing stands empty.

5–13%below reference values of €1.42M to €1.53M for 185 m²

Priced below the market

€7,297 per m² against €7,613 for Berlin's city centre and €8,198 for new-build: 11% below new-build, or €166,630 on this size. An automated valuation for the building shows about €8,059 per m² (estimate, October 2026). That is a building average: it does not price the fifth floor, the skyline view or the roof-terrace access.

185 m² on the fifth floor with access to a roof terrace. Two bedrooms today, and a three-bedroom layout has been drawn up.

Designer value and efficiency

An architect-designed building, entered for a regional architecture award in 2024. Energy class B, district heating. Tiergarten Süd, in a city with 0.3% vacancy.

Reference: Berlin asking rents in 2025 were €20.73/m² for freely financed new-build and €14.90/m² for existing stock. A 115 m² new-build from 2013 next to Park am Gleisdreieck is listed at €22.04/m² cold, and an automated valuation for this building shows about €23/m² (estimate, October 2026). Berlin rent-cap rules can limit the starting rent for buildings first let before October 2014; the scenarios assume market-level rents and need a legal check. Assumptions: 2% vacancy, €4,440 a year of non-recoverable owner costs, growth applies to rent and value, no financing, before income tax.

How the case holds under pressure

If values fall

With values down 1% a year (−10% over ten years) and rent flat at €20/m², the return is still +0.8% a year, a profit of €261,636. It turns negative only beyond about −1.8% a year, a 17% fall.

Rent rules

The base case assumes €20/m², close to Berlin's new-build asking rent of €20.73. Berlin regulates rents on existing tenancies and re-lets: starting rents on re-letting follow the Berlin rent index plus 10%, and the exact reference for this apartment is confirmed against the index before a rent is agreed. Confirm the position with a Berlin lawyer.

Exit

Berlin saw 12,516 resale apartment transactions in 2025, up 10%. The three-bedroom layout widens the pool of buyers and tenants for a unit of this size.

Reading the numbers fairly. Rents on new lettings have corrected in the short term (median −4.3% on the year to H1 2026, still €18.66 per m²) after very strong growth, and condominium prices are roughly flat against the 2022 peak. The case for buying now rests on the gap between demand and completions, and on buying a scarce product below the new-build benchmark.

Sources: Berlin broker market reports 2026; official Berlin statistics; JLL Residential Market Overview Germany H1 2026; CBRE / Berlin Hyp Housing Market Report Berlin 2026; Senate Chancellery of Berlin, housing plan 2040 progress report (2026).

Buying in Germany

Open to buyers from any country

Buyers from any country buy on the same legal terms as Germans: no residence permit and no extra approval. Notary and land-registry costs run at about 1.5–2% of the price, plus 6% transfer tax in Berlin.
